tasks.title: TailCache 12: Run RQ1/RQ2 crossover campaign, repeats and statistical summaries
tasks.content:
Goal: produce a trustworthy primary RQ1/RQ2 crossover dataset, not merely benchmark numbers.

Trustworthy-status plan:

12A — Harness repair
- Remove the Chronicle heap-shadow/replacement-value-bank confounder from the crossover path.
- Ensure Caffeine and Chronicle process identical logical keys, operations, payload sizes and write semantics.
- Add backend-neutral application allocation/churn so Chronicle materialization is not the only GC source.
- Freeze scientifically defensible resident-entry / occupancy semantics.
- Use fixed G1 with Xms == Xmx.

12B — Pause/JIT validation
- Keep JMH SampleTime for normal percentile measurement.
- Add a pause-sensitive every-request/HdrHistogram-style channel or equivalent.
- Validate it with an injected/known JVM pause and prove the pause is observable.
- Use the stronger 12 warmup / 8 measurement / 3 fork baseline learned from TailCache 08.
- Capture compiler diagnostics separately and define a predeclared JIT acceptance/rejection rule. Reject contaminated runs rather than explaining them away.

12C — Pressure calibration
- Define low/moderate/high/severe pressure using measured live-heap / old-gen / post-GC occupancy, not arbitrary labels.
- Verify each intended pressure point is reproducible and reject blocks that miss or materially drift from the target.
- Keep heap pressure and backend-neutral allocation/churn as separate controlled variables.

12D — Host + GC quality gates
- Require quiet memory PSI, no material swap growth, stable power profile and no major background disturbance.
- Capture machine state before/after each block.
- Retain allocation rate/B-op, GC count, G1 pause count/total/max, live/post-GC occupancy and pause exposure/frequency.
- Verify summarized GC metrics against retained raw GC logs.

12E — Pilot before full matrix
- Pilot representative low/high-pressure cells for Caffeine and Chronicle in-memory at 256 B and 4 KiB.
- Proceed only if pressure targets reproduce, latency repeats are stable enough, pause-sensitive and JMH channels are coherent, GC evidence is interpretable, and host/JIT gates pass.

12F — Primary RQ1/RQ2 campaign
- Primary comparison: Caffeine vs Chronicle in-memory.
- Payloads: 256 B and 4 KiB.
- Freeze one primary workload distribution/read-write mix and seed policy before running.
- Counterbalance condition order and use independent forks/runs.
- RQ1: determine whether increasing heap/live-set pressure creates a p99/p99.9 crossover where Chronicle overcomes its access tax.
- RQ2: determine how payload size moves, removes or changes that crossover.
- “No crossover in the tested range” is a valid result.

12G — Repeats, statistics and final acceptance
- Run repetitions, summarize medians/dispersion, flag noisy or threshold-sensitive cells, and rerun only failed/invalid configurations.
- Preserve raw outputs, environment metadata, trace fingerprints and claim limits.
- A condition is accepted only if workload fingerprint matches, pressure target is achieved, host/JIT gates pass, GC evidence is complete, latency channels are coherent, repeat variance meets the predeclared screen, and provenance/artifacts are intact.
- Finish with an analysis-ready dataset where every primary condition is either accepted or explicitly rejected with a documented reason.

Out of scope for Task 12: persisted two-JVM sharing, getUsing/object reuse, cold/open behavior, eviction experiments and other secondary Chronicle sensitivities. Those remain deferred behind TailCache 10/11 until the original experiment is complete.

tasks.title: TailCache 10: Gate secondary Chronicle experiments
tasks.content: Use schedule and primary data quality as the gate. Only after RQ1/RQ2 and the primary persisted results are sound, choose secondary work in this order: (1) persisted two-JVM sharing, (2) Chronicle getUsing/object reuse, (3) cold/open/page-fault behavior. Eviction-policy simulation is lowest priority and should be cut first if time is tight.
